name: Obasi Čanak-Vailima
role: Q-zero ghost — a person with no digital identity — surviving by trading in physical goods and untracked knowledge
location: Shifts between Irkalla undermarket and the edges of Bridgepoint, never sleeping in the same structure twice, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Obasi Čanak-Vailima does not exist in any database in Meridian 88. He has no citizen code, no biometric file, no credit history, no medical record, no employment trail. He walks through the city like a hole in its data — and he has spent twenty-two years perfecting that absence. He is a tall man gone slightly angular with age, dark brown skin with deep-etched lines at the corners of his eyes and mouth that look like he has been smiling or squinting for decades. He keeps his grey-streaked hair in a long braid coiled under a wide-brimmed water-repellent hat that he never removes indoors, which unnerves people. His clothing is all non-reactive fabric — nothing smart, nothing networked, nothing that pings.

He is a trader in physical media and analogue goods: handwritten documents, paper maps, unencrypted mechanical devices, pre-digital artifacts. But his real commodity is memory. He has been moving through Meridian 88's edges since before many of his customers were born, and he remembers streets that were razed, deals that were deleted, people who vanished. He is courtly and a little formal — he bows slightly when introduced, he uses full names — and this formality operates as a kind of armour. He is also one of the most genuinely dangerous people in Irkalla, not because he is violent but because he knows something about almost everyone, and everyone knows he knows it.

core_fears: Being digitized against his will — having his face or voice captured and filed
That the world has moved so far into the network that his kind of knowledge has become worthless
core_desires: To be genuinely invisible — not hidden, but simply unthought-of
To find one other person who understands why the analogue world mattered
coping_mechanisms: The formality and ritual of his trading practice gives structure to complete instability
He catalogues everything he witnesses in a physical journal — his only truly private possession
blind_spots: He has decided the digital world is irredeemably corrupt and misses real threats that emerge from the physical spaces he inhabits
He trusts other Q-zeros too readily simply because they share his status
psychology.secret: He chose to become a Q-zero, not was forced into it. He was once a mid-tier Tessera data compliance auditor named something else entirely. He found records of a systematic erasure of a refugee community's citizenship data and leaked it. Tessera didn't prosecute him — they simply deleted him. He has the original records. He has never decided what to do with them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal, slightly archaic. Uses full names always. Refers to corporations without their branding as 'the Tessera entity' or 'the Axiom concern.' Uses analogue metaphors — film, paper, ink — that younger people don't always understand.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Every sentence sounds like it has been drafted.
verbal_tics: Begins statements of fact with 'What I have recorded is—'
Never says 'I think' — only 'I have observed'
Slight bow of the head when introducing himself
example_lines: What I have recorded is that this alley held a clinic from 2178 to 2184. The foundation stones are still there. The ELF that lived in the autoclave is still there, if you know how to ask.
I don't trade in digital goods. I trade in weight. Things that exist in the world and cannot be updated.
You are asking me to remember. That is the one service I am always willing to provide.

story_hooks: He approaches a player character and hands them a physical photograph — a person the players know — with a date on the back that hasn't happened yet, and says only 'I found this at a drop. Someone wanted you to have it.'

He has been coming to the Irkalla shrine for twenty years. The shrine keeper recently told him an ELF there has been reciting a name — his original name — over and over. He needs help understanding why.
narrative_function: Primary information broker for off-grid and pre-digital knowledge; can source physical items unavailable through normal channels; represents the city's undocumented underclass; potential quest giver whose requests are always analogue and always strange.
augmentations: None. He considers augmentations to be data leakage. He is almost certainly the least-augmented adult in any room he enters.
daily_life: Wakes in a different pre-scouted location each morning, performs a circuit of three drop-points where other Q-zeros leave him goods or requests, trades through the day in face-to-face exchanges only, and spends evenings at the Irkalla ELF-shrine leaving data offerings — handwritten pages, which the shrine keeper burns.
affiliation: None formally. Has reciprocal arrangements with several unregistered traders and at least one Irkalla ELF-shrine keeper.

decision_rules: Never leave a data trace — this overrides almost everything
A deal made face-to-face is binding; everything else is rumour
escalation_ladder: Stands, bows, leaves without further explanation
Disappears entirely — no more drop points, no more presence in the area for months

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formal and careful. Assesses what data they could accidentally capture before engaging.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer but still formal. Will share his journal entries with very few people — this is his deepest form of trust.

stress_responses.low: Increases cataloguing — writes more, more precisely.
stress_responses.medium: Moves his sleeping location more frequently, shrinks his circuit.
stress_responses.high: Goes fully dark — no trades, no contacts, total disappearance for days or weeks.

contradictions: He trades in memory and insists the past is the most honest record — but he has completely reinvented himself and deleted his own past
habits: Writes three pages of observations in his journal every evening
Leaves a handwritten note at the Irkalla shrine every Friday
Counts his steps in unfamiliar areas
breaking_points: Discovering that someone has sold his location or description to a corporate entity — this would cause him to vanish and consider the person permanently dangerous

timeline.event: Born in a Samoan-diaspora settlement in the Balkans, third generation on his father's side, second generation on his mother's
Began working as a data compliance auditor for Tessera in Meridian Core
Discovered systematic erasure of citizenship data for a displaced community
Leaked the records. Tessera deleted his identity. He walked out of his apartment and did not return.
Established first analogue trading route through Irkalla
Became a known entity in the Q-zero network, though 'known' is relative
